scope: Proposition 8.2 (Nullity forces Selmer dimension) of the manuscript “Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves” (preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 006 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c417858c9fe566da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 62. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the curve, support types, a bound for the number of additional constrained places, and a bound for the dimension of a stationary environment. Partition a finite configuration into blocks with zero cross-M entries, and denote their matrices by Mi. There is a constant depending only on these fixed data such that dimF2 Sel2(E(h) /Q) ≥ X i dimF2 ker Mi − C. (8.7) At a unit coefficient symbol the sum of nullities, and hence the number of singular blocks, is therefore uniformly bounded. The bound works for both coefficient sources and is independent of the moving prime ℓ.
